$comment: THE CANONICAL CAPTURE INDEX for lifecycle-card evidence (cinatra#2821, epic #2784 S9h).
A cell name is a CLAIM. This file is where a claim is answered by a RECORD: the host the
picture declares, the URL it was taken on, the screenshot with its SHA-256, and the anchors
that were counted on that screen, in the frame they were counted in. The rules live in
scripts/ci/lib/capture-record-contract.mjs, and that module also exports the ONE path every
reader resolves. scripts/ci/chat-hitl-evidence-gate.mjs binds every acceptance-manifest cell
that names a host to a record here. An unindexed screenshot counts as zero.
THERE IS ONE OF THIS FILE, and it is read by BOTH gates. scripts/audit/chat-hitl-acceptance-gate.mjs
used to read a second index of its own beside it that also called itself canonical and held no
records -- and that empty one was the capture driver's default output, so an honest capture run
wrote where nothing would ever bind it. That file is retired; its load-bearing prose is the
C1 / C2 paragraph below. The audit half is the STRICTER reader: it adds painted counts, measured
absences, a pinned card instance and frame URLs on top of the contract above. Those extras are
GRADED WHEN PRESENT on a committed record and REQUIRED of what its own driver
(scripts/audit/lib/chat-hitl-capture-driver.mjs) writes, so the strictness lands on the records
that tier makes rather than refusing eight records another honest driver made. The contract above
is the floor for every record either way.
FILE NAMES CARRY NO AUTHORITY. A cell called `__chat_thread__` whose record ended on a run-detail
URL, or whose chat anchors were never asserted, is a mislabeled capture and fails. A PENDING
capture owes its decision controls; a DECIDED one owes their ABSENCE and its own decided summary.
WHAT IS ACTUALLY IN IT, read off the records below rather than remembered: FIFTY-EIGHT
records, on all four hosts. Each group is ONE run of the recorder against a LIVE app on a
lane database, not a hand-assembled set. The A / B / C groups are described here; the V, D,
I, S9b, C, P and SCHEDULE groups arrived with later slices, each described in its own
paragraph below where it has one, and each record carries its own `note`:
A1 / A3 / A4 / A5 - cinatra#2855 (PR #2862), evidence/2855-settled-outcome. A1 is the gate
region on the review page. A3 / A4 / A5 are chat_thread: a real gate PENDING, the same card
SETTLED on its own floor naming its outcome and its decider with no Refresh beside it, and
one that LAPSED rather than being decided.
B1 / B2 / B3 / B4 - cinatra#2852 (PR #2863), evidence/2852-before-after. The re-shot chip
row: every suggestion accepted, then one chip dismissed, with the count line in the decision
floor in both -- B1 / B2 on the page gate region, B3 / B4 in a real transcript.
C1 / C2 / C3 - site_widget - cinatra#2754 (PR #2870), evidence/2754-island-wire. The card
in the embedded conversation column on a genuinely cross-site host page, the same card
with the island expanded, and a NEGATIVE CONTROL with one character of the island
credential flipped. Each of the three was validated by capture-record-contract.mjs and came
back record/ok before it was written here.
This paragraph replaces three that had merged into each other and disagreed: two said the
file was populated and a third, left standing after them, said it was EMPTY ON PURPOSE. It
is not empty, and it has not been chat_thread-only since the C-series arrived.
MIND THE C1 / C2 NAMES. The site_widget C1 and C2 here are NOT the chat_thread C1 and C2 the
acceptance manifest cites from evidence/2573-s7-visuals-lane. Those two cells are still
UNBOUND and the gate is still honestly red for them. The S7 run observed THREE of the four
anchors a chat_thread record owes -- the /chat URL class, data-lifecycle-card-host=chat_thread,
and the card root, pending and decided respectively -- and never looked for
[data-conversation-list]. A record asserting a count for an anchor nobody measured is the
fabrication this index exists to refuse, so writing one would be inventing an observation
nobody made. Adopting the pictures above under their names, on the strength of a shared C1,
would be exactly the mislabel this index exists to refuse. They stay grandfathered findings
in the rollout policy until that re-capture happens.
THE page_gate_region RECORDS ARE HERE NOW (cinatra#2791). #2862 photographed the review
page's gate region once (A1) and #2863 twice (B1, B2). All three sat in their own lane's
capture-records.json instead, because the contract's `review_page` URL class read
/^\/agents\/reviews/ -- the open-review QUEUE, a navigation-and-volume screen that mounts no
lifecycle card -- while the surface that declares host="page_gate_region" is
/agents/<vendor>/<package>/<runId>/review/<taskId>. No truthful record of this host could
satisfy the class as written, and a picture of the queue would have satisfied it. The defect
was in the class, not in the pictures: the class now matches the shipped route, in the same
spelling the audit half already used, and the three records are registered above exactly as
their evidence directories define them -- same bytes, same hashes.
A record is TEXT, and text is forgeable: a person can hand-write one with a real image and
invented counts. What the contract does catch is the accidental mislabel, the anchor nobody
measured, the drifted hash, the re-used picture, and the cell that cites nothing at all.
THE P-GROUP - cinatra#2904, evidence/2904-settled-gate-review-page. FIVE records on page_gate_region,
all of them the review page's own gate region at /agents/<vendor>/<package>/<runId>/review/<taskId>.
P1 is the PENDING control: a gate this lane produced through materializeBlogPostBodyArtifact -> the
produced-event outbox -> the app's own review-orchestration sweep, with its live decision floor. P2 and
P4 are two OTHER real gates on their own runs, decided by a real press of the card's own Approve /
Reject control in the browser and then RELOADED, so the route's server loader ran again on a gate it
found RESOLVED - which is the whole point of the round: before #2904 that loader answered `blocked` for
every non-pending gate and the page returned its own panel before the card was mounted, so all three
host anchors counted ZERO here (recorded verbatim in the refusal set of the round that found this, cell
G4__review-card__page_gate_region__decided). P3 and P5 are the same two decided gates opened fresh on
the dark ground; each record carries the class the document actually resolved, so the cell name is not
the only thing claiming the theme.
WHAT IS NOT IN THE P-GROUP, and why it is not a gap. The `unavailable` case - a review-page address for
a gate that was never emitted - draws NO lifecycle card at all, by design (#2904 AC 5). It cannot be a
record in this file, because every record here is a measurement of a card, and asking the recorder for
one would be asking it to measure a card that must not exist. Those two pictures (P6 / P7) and their
counted anchors live in the round's own capture-results.json and its README grading table instead,
where they read as what they are: a negative control.
THE SCHEDULE GROUP - cinatra#2788 (PR #2939, S9d), evidence/2788-s9d-schedule-card. TEN records
of the SCHEDULE card, drawn where the S1 placeholder box used to stand: `trigger_schedule_proposal`
dispatches to the drawn ScheduleProposalCard now and the shell is RETIRED for this kind, so no
record here shows the shell's one-line grey box.
A1 / A2 - chat_thread, ONE continuous interaction in ONE real transcript. A1 is the schedule as
it arrives: the question, the three option rows with the RECURRING row chosen and owning its
fields, the estimated duration, and a floor holding Confirm and nothing else. The rows are LIVE
on first paint and there is NO Adjust control on any phase - the reader edits the rows as they
stand. A2 is the SAME card after a real press of Confirm and a full route reload: no second card,
same place, the armed schedule in the SAME rows, with Save changes to re-arm. Cancel trigger and
Release now are absent - the plan puts those on the run page's schedule step, not in the
conversation.
B1 / B2 - those same two cells on the DARK ground, in a SECOND transcript with a schedule of its
own, because a proposal token is single-use and the A pair spent theirs.
R1 / R2 - run_card, light and dark. The SAME component on the run page, mounted as a DEDICATED
STEP in the left step rail (packages/agents/src/schedule-rail-step.tsx) and opened by a real
press, above the run's other steps and above the Review step. Inside it: the trigger's own chrome
(Trigger configuration, Steps held until trigger fires), the armed schedule in the same option
rows, and a floor with Save changes, Cancel trigger and Release now.
P1 / P2 - page_gate_region, light and dark, on the review page. The schedule is a step in the
left rail ABOVE the Review step, and the gate region beside it holds the REVIEW CARD ALONE. The
two are never drawn together as cards - that composition is the one the plan forbids and the one
the retired page_gate_region schedule mount used to draw.
E1 / E2 - the EXPIRED face, and the ONE STAND-IN in the set. This branch's resolver still answers
an expired proposal `absent` (the vanish defect cinatra#2836 owns), so the expired PHASE cannot be
reached through the server here. The card, the transcript, the browser and every counted anchor
are REAL; what is stood in is the RESOLVE RESPONSE. Both cell names carry `standin` and both notes
say so in words. The reading they prove is the plan's: the card STAYS VISIBLE, its rows stay
EDITABLE, and the floor is Confirm - to set the schedule again.
